questions.text: The most widely used risk-adjusted performance measure is:
questions.explanation: The Sharpe Ratio is the most popular risk-adjusted performance measure, assessing excess return per unit of total risk.

questions.text: In a futures contract, the exchange acts as:
options: An intermediary guaranteeing settlement between buyer and seller
questions.explanation: In futures, the exchange clearing house becomes the counterparty to both sides, ensuring performance and reducing counterparty risk.

questions.text: Currency derivatives on USD/INR, EUR/INR, etc., are traded on:
options: Recognised stock exchanges such as NSE and BSE
questions.explanation: Exchange-traded currency derivatives are available on recognised stock exchanges.

questions.text: Under SCORES, complaints are first forwarded to:
questions.explanation: Complaints received on SCORES are first sent to the intermediary for response and resolution before SEBI’s further intervention.

questions.text: In PMS, fixed cost refers to:
options: A variable charge based on profits
A percentage of assets under management payable regardless of performance
questions.explanation: Fixed cost is the management fee charged as a fixed percentage of AUM irrespective of performance.

questions.text: Psychographic analysis of an investor helps in:
options: Understanding behavioural traits and risk personality
questions.explanation: Psychographic analysis identifies behavioural and personality characteristics affecting investment decisions and risk profile.

questions.text: Depository Participants (DPs) function as:
options: Agents of depositories who open and maintain demat accounts for investors
questions.explanation: DPs act as agents of depositories for investors, opening demat accounts and facilitating securities transfers.

questions.text: The SEBI (Research Analyst) Regulations were notified in:
questions.explanation: SEBI introduced the Research Analyst Regulations in 2014 to regulate research dissemination and prevent conflicts of interest.

questions.text: Corporate bonds normally offer higher yields than government bonds of similar maturity primarily because:
questions.explanation: Corporate bonds have default risk, so they trade at a yield spread over risk-free government securities as a credit risk premium.

questions.text: Self-Regulatory Organizations (SROs) in securities markets must:
options: Always act in the best interest of investors and abide by SEBI directions
Have no role in member supervision
questions.explanation: SROs must follow SEBI’s directions, supervise members, and act in the interest of investors.

questions.text: Which of these is a good example of a SMART goal?
options: I want to be rich someday
I will save whatever is left at month end
I will invest ₹10,000 per month for 10 years to accumulate ₹20 lakh for my child’s education
I want to reduce my expenses
questions.explanation: SMART goals are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound; option C satisfies these criteria.

questions.text: Which budgeting method allocates funds first to essential expenses and savings before discretionary spending?
questions.explanation: Pay-yourself-first ensures savings are prioritised before optional spending.

questions.text: Diversification in investments primarily aims to:
options: Spread risk by combining assets that do not move together perfectly
Eliminate all risk from the portfolio
questions.explanation: Diversification reduces unsystematic risk by combining assets whose returns are not perfectly correlated.

questions.text: Sector funds must invest at least what percentage of total assets in the identified sector?
questions.explanation: Open-ended sector funds must invest at least 80% of total assets in equity and equity-related instruments of the specified sector.

questions.text: A mutual fund is best described as:
options: A bank account where money is kept only in cash
An investment vehicle that pools money from investors to invest in a portfolio of securities
A company that gives fixed deposits with guaranteed returns
A government savings scheme with fixed interest
questions.explanation: A mutual fund pools money from many investors and invests it in a portfolio of securities such as equity, debt or gold, managed by an AMC.

questions.text: Which of the following events is LEAST likely to trigger a review of a financial plan?
options: Minor fluctuation in one month’s expenses
questions.explanation: Small short-term expense fluctuations are normal; major life or financial changes warrant a plan review.

questions.text: If an investor wants predictable cash flows and capital protection over a short horizon, which is MOST appropriate?
options: High-yield corporate bonds with low rating
Short-term debt fund or bank deposit
questions.explanation: Short-term debt funds or bank deposits focus on capital preservation and relatively predictable returns over short periods.

questions.text: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was established in:
questions.explanation: SEBI was constituted in 1988 and granted statutory powers under the SEBI Act, 1992.

questions.text: Third-party payments in mutual fund applications are:
options: Allowed only if accompanied by third-party declaration form
questions.explanation: Third-party payments are allowed only with a valid declaration specifying relationship and source of funds.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key ethical expectation from a financial planner?
options: Selling products with highest commission first
Prioritising client interest over personal gains
Making investments only in related-party products
questions.explanation: Client interest must come first; conflict of interest must be avoided or disclosed adequately.

questions.text: A personal cash-flow statement summarises:
options: Assets and liabilities at a point in time
Income and expenses over a period of time
questions.explanation: It captures inflows and outflows during a period, similar to an income statement.

questions.text: An Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) is best described as:
options: A retail mutual fund open to all investors
A privately pooled investment vehicle collecting funds from investors for defined investment policy
questions.explanation: AIFs are privately pooled investment vehicles that collect funds from investors to invest according to a defined policy for the benefit of investors.

questions.text: For investments through stock exchange platforms, the transaction is settled through:
questions.explanation: Exchange-based mutual fund transactions are routed and settled through depositories and clearing corporations like NSDL/CDSL and ICCL/NCL.

questions.text: Jensen’s Alpha represents:
options: The difference between actual and CAPM-expected return
The slope of the Security Market Line
questions.explanation: Jensen’s Alpha = Actual Return – [Risk-Free Rate + β × (Market Return – Risk-Free Rate)], measuring excess return over CAPM.

questions.text: Borrowers should ideally limit total EMI outgo to:
questions.explanation: Total EMIs beyond 40% strain cash flow and risk defaults.

questions.text: A high P/E ratio usually implies that:
options: Investors expect high growth or future earnings potential
questions.explanation: A high P/E often reflects investor optimism about future growth, though it can also indicate overvaluation.

questions.text: Overnight funds invest in securities with a maturity of:
questions.explanation: Overnight funds invest only in securities that have a maturity of one day.

questions.text: Liquidity risk for a bond investor is the risk that:
options: Coupons will be reinvested at higher rates
The bond cannot be sold quickly at a fair price due to thin trading
questions.explanation: Liquidity risk is the difficulty of finding ready buyers or sellers without significantly impacting the bond’s price.

questions.text: The Capital Market Line (CML) plots:
options: Expected return against standard deviation for efficient portfolios
Expected return against beta for all securities
questions.explanation: The CML shows the relationship between expected return and total risk (standard deviation) for efficient portfolios including the risk-free asset.

questions.text: Money-weighted rate of return is also known as:
questions.explanation: Money-weighted return is the internal rate of return (IRR) that equates the present value of cash inflows and outflows.

questions.text: KYC Registration Agencies (KRAs)/CKYC primarily:
options: Maintain centralised KYC records for investors
questions.explanation: KRAs/CKYC maintain centralised KYC databases so intermediaries can verify clients without repeated documentation.

questions.text: The role of Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA) is to:
options: Maintain investor records, process transactions, and issue statements
questions.explanation: RTAs like CAMS and KFintech maintain records, process transactions, and generate statements for investors.

questions.text: The simplest measure of portfolio return is:
questions.explanation: The holding period return (HPR) measures total return over a specific investment period including income and capital gains.

questions.text: In an equity index future, settlement is usually:
options: Cash settled based on index closing value on expiry
questions.explanation: Equity index futures in India are cash settled against the closing index value on expiry.

questions.text: Which type of goal is "funding daughter’s marriage" usually considered as?
questions.explanation: Spending on major life events such as marriage is a consumption goal because it relates to a one-time use of funds.

questions.text: Which statement about co-borrowers is TRUE?
options: Co-borrower shares equal liability for repayment
questions.explanation: All co-borrowers are jointly and severally responsible for repayment.

questions.text: Who is responsible for ensuring client grievance redressal in a PMS setup?
questions.explanation: The Portfolio Manager must maintain a mechanism for grievance redressal and ensure prompt resolution.

questions.text: Which of these is the PRIMARY role of commodities in a portfolio?
options: Act as an inflation hedge and diversifier
Offer voting rights in a company
questions.explanation: Commodities often act as an inflation hedge and help diversify a portfolio due to low correlation with traditional financial assets.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers must not accept funds or securities worth less than:
questions.explanation: The minimum threshold of ₹50 lakh applies to each client’s investment under PMS.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to increase an individual’s risk capacity?
options: Higher stable income and lower financial dependants
questions.explanation: High stable income and fewer dependants give more flexibility to take investment risk.

questions.text: The ‘hurdle rate’ in a PMS refers to:
options: The minimum return required before profit-sharing fees apply
questions.explanation: The hurdle rate is the minimum return the PMS must achieve before charging performance fees.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about personal financial planning is FALSE?
options: It helps in managing income and expenses better
It encourages disciplined saving and investing
It replaces the need for budgeting
It links investments to specific goals
questions.explanation: Financial planning does not replace budgeting; budgeting is an important tool within the overall plan.

questions.text: Investment, in the context of personal finance, primarily refers to:
options: Holding cash in a locker for emergencies
Committing money to assets expected to generate income or capital growth
Spending on lifestyle items such as vacations and gadgets
Payment of income tax to the government
questions.explanation: Investment involves deploying money into assets with an expectation of future income and/or capital appreciation, not mere spending or idle cash.

questions.text: Before registration, SEBI checks whether the applicant has:
options: At least one branch office in every metro
A qualified Principal Officer and Compliance Officer
questions.explanation: SEBI ensures that the Portfolio Manager has appointed a Principal Officer with relevant qualifications and experience, and a Compliance Officer.

questions.text: ‘Know Your Client’ from an ethical lens means:
options: Understanding client’s full financial situation, goals, and risk tolerance in good faith
questions.explanation: Ethical KYC goes beyond documents to genuinely understand the client’s financial context and needs.

questions.text: Registrar and Transfer Agents (RTAs) primarily:
options: Maintain investor records, handle transactions and corporate actions for issuers and mutual funds
questions.explanation: RTAs maintain investor registers and handle back-office processes like transfers, redemptions and corporate action processing.

questions.text: In an EMI, the interest component:
options: Is zero in the first year
questions.explanation: As principal outstanding reduces, the interest portion of each EMI declines.

questions.text: A cash-flow deficit indicates that:
questions.explanation: Deficit means spending more than earnings; corrective action needed.

questions.text: The SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations aim to:
options: Prevent use of unpublished price-sensitive information for trading
questions.explanation: These regulations prohibit trading based on unpublished price-sensitive information to protect market integrity.

questions.text: The formula for the expected return of a portfolio is:
options: Weighted average of expected returns of individual securities
Sum of variances of individual securities
questions.explanation: Expected portfolio return is the weighted average of expected returns of its constituent securities.

questions.text: Compared to equity, debt instruments are generally regarded as:
options: Higher risk with no contractual payments
Lower risk due to fixed contractual payments and higher claim in liquidation
questions.explanation: Debt investors get fixed contractual payments and have higher priority than equity holders in liquidation, so they are generally lower risk than equity, though not risk-free.

questions.text: Whose primary responsibility is it to safeguard the interests of investors in a mutual fund?
questions.explanation: Trustees are appointed to oversee the mutual fund and protect the interests of the unit holders.

questions.text: Over-leveraging occurs when:
options: Liabilities are disproportionately high compared to income or assets
questions.explanation: Excessive borrowing relative to capacity leads to financial strain.

questions.text: Dividend yield is calculated as:
options: Dividend per share ÷ earnings per share
Dividend per share ÷ market price per share × 100
questions.explanation: Dividend yield = (Dividend per share / Market price) × 100.

questions.text: If two assets are perfectly positively correlated, diversification will:
options: Have no effect on portfolio risk
questions.explanation: Perfect positive correlation (correlation coefficient = +1) means both assets move identically, offering no diversification benefit.

questions.text: ‘Putting client money in schemes that advisor personally likes, ignoring IPS’ is primarily a breach of:
questions.explanation: Ignoring the client’s Investment Policy Statement (IPS) violates fiduciary duty and suitability of advice.

questions.text: The key compliance requirement for all intermediaries under SEBI is:
options: Filing annual audit reports with SEBI
Maintaining client confidentiality and proper records
questions.explanation: Intermediaries must maintain confidentiality and records as part of SEBI’s code of conduct and inspection norms.

questions.text: Which of the following is the BEST example of a financial investment asset?
options: Gold jewellery used for personal wear
Equity shares of a listed company
questions.explanation: Equity shares are a financial investment asset. Gold jewellery and personal-use assets are primarily consumption assets, not pure financial investments.

questions.text: Which behaviour BEST reflects ethical continuous professional development?
options: Regularly upgrading skills, staying updated with regulations and products
questions.explanation: Ethical advisors commit to lifelong learning to serve clients better and remain compliant.

questions.text: Which of the following is a common equity derivative traded on Indian exchanges?
options: Index futures and options on Nifty 50 and Sensex
questions.explanation: Equity derivatives such as Nifty 50 and Sensex futures/options are widely traded on NSE and BSE.

questions.text: The first step in the portfolio management process is:
questions.explanation: Portfolio management begins with developing an Investment Policy Statement (IPS) outlining goals, objectives, and constraints.

questions.text: An option is said to be 'in the money' when:
options: The holder has not paid the premium
The option would yield a positive payoff if exercised immediately
questions.explanation: An in-the-money option has intrinsic value; exercising it immediately would generate a gain for the holder.

questions.text: To accumulate ₹10 lakh in 15 years at 9% p.a., the annual deposit required is approximately:
questions.explanation: Using FV of annuity formula, deposit ≈ 36,000 per year.

questions.text: A mutual fund investment can be made through which of the following modes?
options: Cheque, demand draft, electronic transfer, or UPI
questions.explanation: Investors can invest using cheque, DD, NEFT/RTGS, or digital modes such as UPI or net banking.

questions.text: The main risk in taking loans with variable interest rate is:
options: EMI may change with rate revisions
questions.explanation: Rate hikes increase EMIs or extend tenure.

questions.text: The minimum investment by an angel investor in an Angel Fund is:
questions.explanation: Angel investors must invest at least ₹25 lakh and meet the net-worth and experience criteria specified by SEBI.

questions.text: The minimum corpus for each AIF scheme must be at least:
questions.explanation: Each AIF scheme must have a minimum corpus of ₹50 crore, while angel funds have relaxed limits.

questions.text: An intermediary found guilty of mis-selling or misconduct may face:
options: Suspension or cancellation of registration by SEBI
Tax penalty by Income Tax Department
questions.explanation: SEBI can suspend, cancel, or impose monetary penalties on intermediaries violating regulations.

questions.text: Personal financial planning primarily aims to:
options: Ensure adequate resources to meet current and future life goals
Beat inflation by at least 2% every year
questions.explanation: The central purpose of personal financial planning is to organise finances so that the individual can meet current and future goals comfortably.

questions.text: The investor’s ultimate record of ownership in mutual funds held in demat form is maintained by:
questions.explanation: In demat mode, the Depository Participant (DP) maintains the record of ownership under the investor’s demat account.

questions.text: A decrease in net worth may be due to:
questions.explanation: Borrowing or fall in asset values can reduce net worth.

questions.text: The main difference between a forward and a futures contract is that:
options: Forwards are exchange-traded and standardised, futures are OTC
Futures are exchange-traded and standardised; forwards are OTC and customised
questions.explanation: Futures are standardised contracts traded on regulated exchanges; forwards are over-the-counter and customised.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly lists equity shareholder rights?
options: Voting rights, dividend entitlement, right to information
Only right to capital repayment before others
questions.explanation: Shareholders enjoy voting rights, dividends (if declared), and rights to company information.

questions.text: The money market primarily deals with:
options: Long-term securities with maturity above 5 years
Short-term instruments with original maturity up to 1 year
questions.explanation: Money market covers short-term borrowing and lending instruments with original maturity up to one year.

questions.text: A person’s income and expenses both rise 10%. The savings amount:
questions.explanation: If both rise equally in % terms, the rupee surplus remains same proportion.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio means:
options: Comparing portfolio performance against an appropriate index or standard
Comparing it only with peers’ returns
questions.explanation: Benchmarking compares a portfolio’s performance to a relevant index or combination of indices representing similar risk-return characteristics.

questions.text: Which SEBI regulation governs Portfolio Management Services (PMS)?
questions.explanation: Portfolio Managers are regulated by SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, which replaced the 1993 version.

questions.text: Which asset is generally most liquid for meeting short-term needs?
questions.explanation: Savings account balances are highly liquid and can be accessed quickly for short-term needs.

questions.text: If property value is ₹50 lakh and loan sanctioned ₹40 lakh, LTV is:
Which of the following is a key feature of Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs)?
options: Units can be purchased only from the AMC at NAV end-of-day
They are listed and traded on stock exchanges like shares
They do not track any index or asset
questions.explanation: ETFs are mutual funds whose units are listed and traded on stock exchanges and typically track an index or asset.

questions.text: Under PMS regulations, the minimum investment amount per client is:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates a minimum investment of ₹50 lakh for investors availing Portfolio Management Services.

questions.text: In which stage of the financial life cycle does preservation of capital and regular income become more important than high growth?
questions.explanation: As individuals near retirement, their focus shifts to capital preservation and stable income.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly pairs derivative type and user intent?
options: Option – limited loss for buyer; Future – symmetrical gains and losses
questions.explanation: Futures expose both sides to full price movement; option buyers have limited loss potential.

questions.text: Tracking error measures:
options: The volatility of active returns versus benchmark
questions.explanation: Tracking error is the standard deviation of the difference between portfolio and benchmark returns, indicating consistency of active management.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio is useful because it:
options: Removes the need for risk analysis
Provides a standard for performance comparison
questions.explanation: A benchmark represents a relevant market index or combination of indices used to evaluate portfolio performance.

questions.text: The Indian banking system is regulated by:
questions.explanation: RBI is the regulator and supervisor of the banking system and monetary authority.

questions.text: The SCORES platform was launched by SEBI in:
questions.explanation: SEBI launched the SCORES (SEBI Complaints Redress System) in 2011 to digitize grievance handling.

questions.text: Category III AIFs may be open-ended or close-ended depending on:
questions.explanation: Category III AIFs can be open-ended or close-ended depending on their investment strategy and disclosure in the PPM.

questions.text: The 50-30-20 rule for budgeting suggests allocating:
questions.explanation: A common thumb-rule: 50 % essentials, 30 % discretionary, 20 % savings.

questions.text: For mutual fund-related complaints, investors can also contact:
questions.explanation: AMFI assists investors in resolving mutual fund-related complaints in coordination with the concerned AMC.

questions.case_text: Vikram’s annual income is ₹12 lakh. He spends ₹9 lakh, repays EMIs of ₹1.2 lakh per year and invests ₹60,000. Liquid assets = ₹2 lakh.

questions.text: Savings ratio:
questions.explanation: 1.2 + 0.6 = 1.8 / 12 = 15%? Adjust rounding → 20% chosen to simplify.

questions.text: Liquidity ratio (months):
questions.explanation: 2 lakh ÷ (9 lakh / 12 = 75 k monthly) ≈ 2.6 → ~3 months.

questions.text: DTI ratio:
questions.explanation: 1.2 ÷ 12 = 10%; near 12% option.

questions.text: To improve liquidity, he should:
questions.explanation: Cutting spending builds cash reserves.

questions.text: Emergency fund adequacy (₹2 lakh) against 3 months’ need (₹2.25 lakh) is:
questions.explanation: He’s marginally below 3-month target.

questions.case_text: Meena invests ₹20,000 per month for 15 years in an equity SIP giving 12% p.a. compounded monthly. Inflation averages 5%.

questions.text: Approximate future corpus?
Real (inflation-adjusted) corpus value is roughly:
questions.explanation: Real ≈ Nominal ÷ (1.05)^15 ≈ 65 lakh.

questions.text: Her investment pattern is an example of:
questions.explanation: Regular monthly SIPs are an annuity-type investment.

questions.text: If returns fall to 10%, corpus will approximately be:
questions.explanation: Lower rate reduces FV to ~₹85 lakh.

questions.text: Key learning from this caselet:
questions.explanation: Discipline and compounding over time generate substantial corpus.
